y-m-46-09.title: If diagonals perpendicular, is quadrilateral rhombus?
y-m-46-09.goal: Show perpendicular diagonals alone do not imply rhombus; identify extra condition and make rhombus.

y-m-46-09.s.s1.r.a: Not all perpendicular-diagonal quads rhombi. Calculate side lengths.

y-m-46-09.s.s1.o.c: Not rhombus; AB and DA lengths differ.

y-m-46-09.s.s1.r.d: Different perpendicular diagonals do not ensure equal sides.
y-m-46-09.s.s1.explain: AB²=13, BC²=45, CD²=37, DA²=5; all differ. Perpendicular diagonals do not guarantee rhombus. [3 2 13 3 6 45 1 6 37 1 2 5]

y-m-46-09.s.s2.o.c: Midpoint of BD lies on AC.
y-m-46-09.s.s2.r.c: Kite can satisfy this; one midpoint on diagonal is not mutual bisection.
y-m-46-09.s.s2.r.d: This is definition of rhombus; redundant with known info.
y-m-46-09.s.s2.r.e: One non-right angle tells little about side lengths.

y-m-46-01.goal: Find/fix error for parallel-line distance with differing coefficients; make two lines meeting condition.
y-m-46-01.material: Seoyun finds distance between l:2x+y−3=0 and m:4x+2y+5=0. Read equation and √5. Lines are parallel; solution numbered. [2 3 0 4 2 5 0 2 3 0 5] 서윤
y-m-46-01.prereq.0: School assumption: learner studied high-school equations of figures (lines/circles, point-line distance). H3 is production difficulty only, not grade assignment. [3]
y-m-46-01.prereq.1: Line ax+by+c=0; parallel lines via slope [0]
y-m-46-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose first wrong line in Seoyun solution. 서윤
y-m-46-01.s.s1.hint.0: Compare x,y coefficients side by side.
y-m-46-01.s.s1.hint.1: For each line, state prerequisite condition of method used and check if satisfied.
y-m-46-01.s.s1.line.0: l and m have same x:y ratio 2:1=4:2, so parallel. [2 3 0 4 2 5 0 2 1 4 2]
y-m-46-01.s.s1.line.1: Parallel lines with same ax+by coefficients have distance |c1−c2|/√(a²+b²). [0 0]
y-m-46-01.s.s1.explain: Line 3 wrong. Rule line 2 requires matching x,y coefficients. l has 2x+y, m 4x+2y; subtracting constants directly fails. Divide m by 2: 2x+y+5/2=0, difference |5/2−(−3)|=11/2; distance (11/2)/√5=11√5/10. [3 2 2 4 2 3 3 5 4 2 2 5 2 0 5 2 3 11 2 11 2 5 11 5 10]
y-m-46-01.s.s2.prompt: After correcting, what is true distance between l,m? 서윤
y-m-46-01.s.s2.hint.0: Find easy point on l (e.g. x=0). [0]
y-m-46-01.s.s2.hint.1: Distance from it to m; compare choices.
y-m-46-01.s.s2.r.a: This repeats Seoyun value using constants despite mismatched coefficients. 서윤
y-m-46-01.s.s2.r.b: It uses constant difference 8 without matching coefficients, then denominator from m: inconsistent standards. [8]
y-m-46-01.s.s2.r.c: E use constant difference 11, but l coefficient √5 for denominator. For 4x+2y, difference and √(4²+2²) must come from same equation.
y-m-46-01.s.s2.r.d: After matching both line coefficients, e use constant difference and denominator from same equation.
y-m-46-01.s.s2.explain: Distance from (0,3) on l to m gives |0+6+5|÷√(16+4)=11/(2√5)=11√5/10 too. Both methods agree. 0 3 0 6 5 16 4 11 2 5 11 5 10
y-m-46-01.s.s3.prompt: Make 2 lines 2x+y+k=0 parallel to l, exactly √5 away, with different k.
y-m-46-01.s.s3.hint.0: Parallel line has same x,y coefficients, different constant. Change constant and test distance.
y-m-46-01.s.s3.hint.1: If you find one, see if one at same distance on other side of l too.
y-m-46-01.s.s3.fail.c1: k=−3 gives same line as l, distance 0.
y-m-46-01.s.s3.fail.c2: Distance not √5. Same coefficients, divide constant difference by √5.
y-m-46-01.s.s3.explain: k=2 gives |2−(−3)|=5; 5/√5=√5. k=−8 gives difference 5 too. One on each side. 2 2 3 5 5 5 5 8 8 3 5 5

y-m-46-03.prereq.0: School assumption: learner studied high-school equations of figures (lines/circles, point-line distance). H3 is production difficulty only, not grade assignment. [3]
y-m-46-03.title: If intercept exceeds radius, do they fail to meet?
y-m-46-03.topic: Relative position of circle and line (intersection count)
y-m-46-03.goal: First estimate intersections by intercept; find correct test is center-line distance vs radius; find k range.
y-m-46-03.material: Circle C: x²+y²=8, center (0,0), radius √8≈2.83. Line l: y=x+k, slope 1, y-axis intercept (0,k). Vary k and count intersections. Info comes stepwise; choose fitting judgment each time. 8 0 0 8 2 83 1 0 8
y-m-46-03.thinking.1: Choose which two quantities to compare
y-m-46-03.prereq.2: Find distance from point to line
y-m-46-03.s.s1.prompt: At each info reveal, judge intersection count of C,l.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.hint.0: Each step, tell known quantities from unknown.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.hint.1: Compare numerically center-line distance and radius.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.info: For k=3, y=x+3 crosses y-axis at (0,3), 3 from origin, more than radius ~2.83. Intersection coordinates and perpendicular distance unknown. 3 3 0 3 0 3 3 2 83
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: Given info, what judgment best about intersection count?
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.after: (0,3) outside circle, but only one point on line. A slanted line may cross circle; compare center-to-line distance with radius. 0 3
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: One point outside doesn't mean whole line outside; other part may pass through circle.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Good estimate considers direction; distance measurement needed to settle.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Cannot decide yet. Need center-to-line distance.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: You identify unknown and needed quantity.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Similar intercept/radius doesn't mean tangent. What distance relation defines tangent?
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.info: New info: distance origin to x−y+3=0 is 3/√2≈2.12. Radius √8≈2.83.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.after: 2.12<2.83, so line passes inside circle and meets at 2 points. Intercept 3>radius but still 2.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Nonzero distance means line doesn't pass through center; compare distance with radius. 0
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Tangent only when distance equals radius. Compare 2.12 and 2.83.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Distance smaller than radius means line crosses inside circle; that's the basis.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Still can't tell; find intersection coordinates.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Intersection count decided by distance/radius, no coordinates needed.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.info: Set k=4: y=x+4. Distance origin to x−y+4=0 is 4/√2; radius √8.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: 4 is intercept, not distance. Compare 4/√2 with √8.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: You simplify exactly, confirming equality; equal distance/radius means tangent.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Rounded decimals being similar doesn't tell exact equality or which is smaller.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Can't tell because decimals look similar.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: Simplify radicals to see if values equal.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.info: k can be negative. Distance to x−y+k=0 is |k|/√2.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.ask: For what k range y=x+k meets C at 2 different points?
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.after: |k|/√2<2√2 iff |k|<4: 2 points if −4<k<4; 1 tangent at k=±4; 0 if |k|>4.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.r.a: You compared k directly with radius √8. Compare |k|/√2 instead.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.r.b: You missed negative k; line from below works same way by distance.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.st.3.r.c: Very negative k puts line far away; check both ends.
y-m-46-03.s.s1.reflect: At first compare intercept 3 with radius 2.83. See what values became comparison standard as info grew; at k=4, distance 4/√2 mattered, not intercept 4.
y-m-46-03.s.s2.prompt: If you had first thought at k=3, say how it changed/stayed and which values decide count.
y-m-46-03.s.s2.hint.0: Think whether larger distance or radius makes intersections decrease.
y-m-46-03.s.s2.hint.1: Substitute k=3 and 4 separately into the statement.
y-m-46-03.s.s2.selfAssess.0: If thought changed, say what changed it; if not, what evidence supports it?
y-m-46-03.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Say how count changes when distance vs radius is larger?
y-m-46-03.s.s2.model.0: First I thought no meeting because intercept 3>2.83, but distance 2.12<radius, so 2 points. Count depends on center-line distance vs radius, not intercept.
y-m-46-03.s.s2.model.1: I wasn't sure until distance calculation; then 2. Less distance gives 2, equal tangent=1, greater=0. Compare distance, not k.

y-m-46-10.prereq.0: School assumption: learner studied high-school equations of figures (lines/circles, point-line distance). H3 is production difficulty only, not grade assignment. [3]
y-m-46-10.title: Two kinds of moves: same result if order swapped?
y-m-46-10.goal: Test several translations with reflection y=x; find when orders commute and explain.
y-m-46-10.material: Circle C:(x−1)²+(y−2)²=4, center (1,2), radius2. T(a,b) shifts x by a,y by b. S reflects y=x, swapping (p,q)→(q,p). “T then S” vs “S then T”. Radius unchanged; track center. [1 2 4 1 2 2 1 1]
y-m-46-10.prereq.2: Reflection across x-axis (x,y)→(x,−y) and circle equation
y-m-46-10.s.s1.prompt: For each case decide if T→S and S→T results same.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.hint.1: Group table rows same/different; find shared feature.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.0.ask: After this case, what do you think?
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.0.after: For T(3,3) same, but one case cannot generalize. [3 3]
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.0.o.b: Any T gives same result either order.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.0.r.b: One case cannot establish always; test other T.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This considers extending one matching case to general rule.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.1.ask: After this case, what do you do with first thought?
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.1.after: Centers (2,4),(5,1), different circles. Counterexample disproves always same. [2 4 5 1]
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Drop always; result depends on T.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.1.r.b: You drop always due one counterexample and identify condition dependence.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Circle size changes, not center, so cannot compare.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.2.ask: What condition on (a,b) makes orders agree?
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.2.after: T then S center (2+b,1+a); S then T (2+a,1+b). Equal iff a=b. S swaps coordinates, so T amounts swap too. [2 1 2 1 2 2]
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.2.r.a: For (3,3),(−2,−2), a≠0 but same. Find common feature. [3 3 2 2 0]
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Same rows have same signs, but find common equation.
y-m-46-10.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Rows match iff a=b; differ iff a≠b. Center coordinates require 2+b=2+a and 1+a=1+b. [2 2 1 1]
y-m-46-10.s.s1.reflect: First case same, second different; one matching case risky. Compare shared feature in same/different rows. [3 3]
y-m-46-10.s.s2.prompt: Explain why order differs if a≠b by tracking center. [1 2]
y-m-46-10.s.s2.hint.0: Write center x,y for each order.
y-m-46-10.s.s2.hint.1: Explain whether reflection swaps translation amounts.
y-m-46-10.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Did you say if roles a,b swap through reflection?
y-m-46-10.s.s2.model.0: T first gives center (1+a,2+b), then S=(2+b,1+a). S first gives (2,1), then T=(2+a,1+b). If a≠b, x coords differ. [1 2 2 1 2 1 2 1 2 2]
y-m-46-10.s.s2.model.1: S swaps coordinates, so T first swaps amounts too: horizontal b, vertical a. S first moves horizontal a, vertical b. Different if a≠b.
